  (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (s : Set A) : Set (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜)
ProjectiveSpectrum.zeroLocus.comment:
The zero locus of a set `s` of elements of a commutative ring `A` is the set of all relevant
homogeneous prime ideals of the ring that contain the set `s`.

An element `f` of `A` can be thought of as a dependent function on the projective spectrum of `𝒜`.
At a point `x` (a homogeneous prime ideal) the function (i.e., element) `f` takes values in the
quotient ring `A` modulo the prime ideal `x`. In this manner, `zeroLocus s` is exactly the subset
of `ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜` where all "functions" in `s` vanish simultaneously.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.ProjectiveSpectrum.asHomogeneousIdeal: This definition introduces a construction that associates a homogeneous ideal to a projective spectrum of a graded algebra.

ProjectiveSpectrum.vanishingIdeal.comment:
The vanishing ideal of a set `t` of points of the projective spectrum of a commutative ring `R`
is the intersection of all the relevant homogeneous prime ideals in the set `t`.

An element `f` of `A` can be thought of as a dependent function on the projective spectrum of `𝒜`.
At a point `x` (a homogeneous prime ideal) the function (i.e., element) `f` takes values in the
quotient ring `A` modulo the prime ideal `x`. In this manner, `vanishingIdeal t` is exactly the
ideal of `A` consisting of all "functions" that vanish on all of `t`.

explanatories.ProjectiveSpectrum.asHomogeneousIdeal: This definition introduces a construction that associates a homogeneous ideal to a projective spectrum of a graded algebra.

explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ: The definition describes how to obtain the germ of a section of a presheaf at a point within an open set, providing a morphism from the section to the stalk at that point.
explanatories.ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen: This definition describes the basic open set in the projective spectrum as the collection of all prime ideals that do not contain a specified element.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.mem_basicOpen_den: This theorem establishes that a point in the projective spectrum is contained in a basic open set defined by a homogeneous element when the element's denominator shares the same degree as the homogeneous ideal associated with that point.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.sectionInBasicOpen: This definition establishes a function that, given a point associated with a homogeneous prime ideal and an element in the homogeneous localization, returns a section in the basic open set defined by the denominator of that element.
explanatories.Quotient.liftOn': This definition describes a variant of a function that processes elements from a quotient type, where the setoid is provided as an implicit argument instead of being an instance.
explanatories.HomogeneousLocalization.NumDenSameDeg.em: This definition establishes a correspondence between a specific structure in homogeneous localization and an element within the localized ring, represented as the fraction of the numerator over the denominator in the context of a given prime ideal.
explanatories.Localization.mk_eq_mk': The theorem asserts that the representations of elements in a localization are equivalent regardless of the specific construction used for the localization, highlighting their consistent nature.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk'_eq_iff_eq: The theorem establishes a biconditional relationship indicating that two localized elements are equal if and only if their corresponding transformations via the algebra map satisfy a specific equality involving their paired components and the elements from the original ring.
explanatories.IsLocalization.eq_iff_exists: The theorem states that the equality of images under the algebra map from a commutative semiring is equivalent to the existence of an element from the submonoid such that multiplying it by each of the original elements yields the same product.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ_ext: The theorem establishes that if two sections of a presheaf agree on a neighborhood from which they are pulled back to a common open set, then their germ representations at a specific point in that open set are also equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.homOfLE: This definition converts an inequality between two elements in a preorder into a morphism in the associated category.
explanatories.inf_le_left: The infimum of two elements is less than or equal to the first element.
explanatories.inf_le_right: The infimum of two elements is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map_units: The theorem states that the image of the algebra map from a commutative semiring to another, when applied to any element from a specific submonoid, is always a unit in the target semiring.
explanatories.IsUnit.mul_left_cancel: If an element in a monoid is a unit, multiplying it on the left by that unit allows one to cancel it out in an equation.
explanatories.map_mul: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

algebraic_geometry.homogeneous_localizat.fullDefinition: def homogeneousLocalizationToStalk (x : ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒜) (y : at x) :     (Proj.structureSheaf 𝒜).presheaf.stalk x := Quotient.liftOn' y (fun f =>   (Proj.structureSheaf 𝒜).presheaf.germ ⟨x, mem_basicOpen_den _ x f⟩ (sectionInBasicOpen _ x f))   fun f g (e : f.embedding = g.embedding) ↦ by     simp only [HomogeneousLocalization.NumDenSameDeg.embedding, Localization.mk_eq_mk',       IsLocalization.mk'_eq_iff_eq,       IsLocalization.eq_iff_exists x.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl] at e     obtain ⟨⟨c, hc⟩, hc'⟩ := e     apply (Proj.structureSheaf 𝒜).presheaf.germ_ext       (ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f.den.1 ⊓         ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 g.den.1 ⊓ ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 c)       ⟨⟨mem_basicOpen_den _ x f, mem_basicOpen_den _ x g⟩, hc⟩       (homOfLE inf_le_left ≫ homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_left ≫ homOfLE inf_le_right)     apply Subtype.ext     ext ⟨t, ⟨htf, htg⟩, ht'⟩     rw [Proj.res_apply, Proj.res_apply]     simp only [sectionInBasicOpen, HomogeneousLocalization.val_mk, Localization.mk_eq_mk',       IsLocalization.mk'_eq_iff_eq]     apply (IsLocalization.map_units (M := t.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl)       (Localization t.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl) ⟨c, ht'⟩).mul_left_cancel     rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul, hc']

WeierstrassCurve.twoTorsionPolynomial.comment:
A cubic polynomial whose discriminant is a multiple of the Weierstrass curve discriminant. If
`W` is an elliptic curve over a field `R` of characteristic different from 2, then its roots over a
splitting field of `R` are precisely the $X$-coordinates of the non-zero 2-torsion points of `W`.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.polynomial.code: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.polynomial.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (W : Affine R) : R[X][Y]
WeierstrassCurve.Affine.polynomial.comment:
The polynomial $W(X, Y) := Y^2 + a_1XY + a_3Y - (X^3 + a_2X^2 + a_4X + a_6)$ associated to a
Weierstrass curve `W` over `R`. For ease of polynomial manipulation, this is represented as a term
of type `R[X][X]`, where the inner variable represents $X$ and the outer variable represents $Y$.
For clarity, the alternative notations `Y` and `R[X][Y]` are provided in the `Polynomial`
scope to represent the outer variable and the bivariate polynomial ring `R[X][X]` respectively.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope.code: WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope.{u} {F : Type u} [Field F] (W : Affine F) (x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ : F) : F
WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope.comment:
The slope of the line through two affine points $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ in `W`.
If $x_1 \ne x_2$, then this line is the secant of `W` through $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$,
and has slope $(y_1 - y_2) / (x_1 - x_2)$. Otherwise, if $y_1 \ne -y_1 - a_1x_1 - a_3$,
then this line is the tangent of `W` at $(x_1, y_1) = (x_2, y_2)$, and has slope
$(3x_1^2 + 2a_2x_1 + a_4 - a_1y_1) / (2y_1 + a_1x_1 + a_3)$. Otherwise, this line is vertical,
and has undefined slope, in which case this function returns the value 0.

This depends on `W`, and has argument order: $x_1$, $x_2$, $y_1$, $y_2$.

explanatories.WeierstrassCurve.a₄: This definition specifies a way to retrieve the fourth coefficient of a Weierstrass curve.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope.fullDefinition: noncomputable def slope {F : Type u} [Field F] (W : Affine F) (x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ : F) : F :=   if x₁ = x₂ then if y₁ = W.negY x₂ y₂ then 0     else (3 * x₁ ^ 2 + 2 * W.a₂ * x₁ + W.a₄ - W.a₁ * y₁) / (y₁ - W.negY x₁ y₁)   else (y₁ - y₂) / (x₁ - x₂)
WeierstrassCurve.Affine.slope.description: This definition specifies a method to calculate the slope of the line connecting two affine points on a Weierstrass curve, distinguishing between secant, tangent, and vertical lines based on their coordinates.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.cyclic_sum_Y_mul_X_sub_X.{u} {F : Type u} [Field F] {W : Affine F} {x₁ x₂ : F} (y₁ y₂ : F)
  (hx : x₁ ≠ x₂) :
  y₁ * (x₂ - W.addX x₁ x₂ (W.slope x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂)) + y₂ * (W.addX x₁ x₂ (W.slope x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂) - x₁) +
      W.negAddY x₁ x₂ y₁ (W.slope x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂) * (x₁ - x₂) =
    0

assuming that P₁ + P₂ + P₃ = O.

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.Nonsingular.comment:
The proposition that a point representative $(x, y, z)$ in `W'` is nonsingular.
In other words, either $W_X(x, y, z) \ne 0$, $W_Y(x, y, z) \ne 0$, or $W_Z(x, y, z) \ne 0$.

Note that this definition is only mathematically accurate for fields.

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.Nonsingular.eq_1.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (W' : Jacobian R) (P : Fin 3 → R) :

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.nonsingular_if.code:
WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.nonsingular_iff.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {W' : Jacobian R} (P : Fin 3 → R) :
  W'.Nonsingular P ↔
    W'.Equation P ∧
      (W'.a₁ * P y * P z - (3 * P x ^ 2 + 2 * W'.a₂ * P x * P z ^ 2 + W'.a₄ * P z ^ 4) ≠ 0 ∨
        2 * P y + W'.a₁ * P x * P z + W'.a₃ * P z ^ 3 ≠ 0 ∨
          W'.a₁ * P x * P y + 3 * W'.a₃ * P y * P z ^ 2 -
              (2 * W'.a₂ * P x ^ 2 * P z + 4 * W'.a₄ * P x * P z ^ 3 + 6 * W'.a₆ * P z ^ 5) ≠
            0)

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.addX.fullDefinition: def addX (P Q : Fin 3 → R) : R :=   P x * Q x ^ 2 * P z ^ 2 - 2 * P y * Q y * P z * Q z + P x ^ 2 * Q x * Q z ^ 2     - W'.a₁ * P x * Q y * P z ^ 2 * Q z - W'.a₁ * P y * Q x * P z * Q z ^ 2     + 2 * W'.a₂ * P x * Q x * P z ^ 2 * Q z ^ 2 - W'.a₃ * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z     - W'.a₃ * P y * P z * Q z ^ 4 + W'.a₄ * Q x * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 2     + W'.a₄ * P x * P z ^ 2 * Q z ^ 4 + 2 * W'.a₆ * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 4
WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.addX.description: This definition specifies how to compute the X-coordinate resulting from the addition of two distinct points on the Jacobian of a Weierstrass curve.

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.addX.eq_1.code:
WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.addX.eq_1.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (W' : Jacobian R) (P Q : Fin 3 → R) :
  W'.addX P Q =
    P x * Q x ^ 2 * P z ^ 2 - 2 * P y * Q y * P z * Q z + P x ^ 2 * Q x * Q z ^ 2 - W'.a₁ * P x * Q y * P z ^ 2 * Q z -
                  W'.a₁ * P y * Q x * P z * Q z ^ 2 +
                2 * W'.a₂ * P x * Q x * P z ^ 2 * Q z ^ 2 -
              W'.a₃ * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z -
            W'.a₃ * P y * P z * Q z ^ 4 +
          W'.a₄ * Q x * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 2 +
        W'.a₄ * P x * P z ^ 2 * Q z ^ 4 +
      2 * W'.a₆ * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 4

  (hP : W'.Equation P) (hQ : W'.Equation Q) :

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.negAddY.fullDefinition: def negAddY (P Q : Fin 3 → R) : R :=   -P y * Q x ^ 3 * P z ^ 3 + 2 * P y * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 3 - 3 * P x ^ 2 * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 2 * Q z     + 3 * P x * P y * Q x ^ 2 * P z * Q z ^ 2 + P x ^ 3 * Q y * Q z ^ 3     - 2 * P y ^ 2 * Q y * Q z ^ 3 + W'.a₁ * P x * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 4     + W'.a₁ * P y * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 3 * Q z - W'.a₁ * P x * P y * Q y * P z * Q z ^ 3     - W'.a₁ * P y ^ 2 * Q x * Q z ^ 4 - 2 * W'.a₂ * P x * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z     + 2 * W'.a₂ * P x * P y * Q x * P z * Q z ^ 4 + W'.a₃ * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 6     - W'.a₃ * P y ^ 2 * Q z ^ 6 - W'.a₄ * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 6 * Q z     - W'.a₄ * P x * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 3 + W'.a₄ * P y * Q x * P z ^ 3 * Q z ^ 4     + W'.a₄ * P x * P y * P z * Q z ^ 6 - 2 * W'.a₆ * Q y * P z ^ 6 * Q z ^ 3     + 2 * W'.a₆ * P y * P z ^ 3 * Q z ^ 6
WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.negAddY.description: This definition describes the Y-coordinate associated with the negation of the sum of two distinct points on a Weierstrass curve's Jacobian.

WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.negAddY.eq_1.code:
WeierstrassCurve.Jacobian.negAddY.eq_1.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (W' : Jacobian R) (P Q : Fin 3 → R) :
  W'.negAddY P Q =
    -P y * Q x ^ 3 * P z ^ 3 + 2 * P y * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 3 - 3 * P x ^ 2 * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 2 * Q z +
                                      3 * P x * P y * Q x ^ 2 * P z * Q z ^ 2 +
                                    P x ^ 3 * Q y * Q z ^ 3 -
                                  2 * P y ^ 2 * Q y * Q z ^ 3 +
                                W'.a₁ * P x * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 4 +
                              W'.a₁ * P y * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 3 * Q z -
                            W'.a₁ * P x * P y * Q y * P z * Q z ^ 3 -
                          W'.a₁ * P y ^ 2 * Q x * Q z ^ 4 -
                        2 * W'.a₂ * P x * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z +
                      2 * W'.a₂ * P x * P y * Q x * P z * Q z ^ 4 +
                    W'.a₃ * Q y ^ 2 * P z ^ 6 -
                  W'.a₃ * P y ^ 2 * Q z ^ 6 -
                W'.a₄ * Q x * Q y * P z ^ 6 * Q z -
              W'.a₄ * P x * Q y * P z ^ 4 * Q z ^ 3 +
            W'.a₄ * P y * Q x * P z ^ 3 * Q z ^ 4 +
          W'.a₄ * P x * P y * P z * Q z ^ 6 -
        2 * W'.a₆ * Q y * P z ^ 6 * Q z ^ 3 +
      2 * W'.a₆ * P y * P z ^ 3 * Q z ^ 6

  (h₁ : W.Equation x₁ y₁) (h₂ : W.Equation x₂ y₂) (hxy : x₁ = x₂ → y₁ ≠ W.negY x₂ y₂) :

      XYIdeal W (W.addX x₁ x₂ (W.slope x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂)) (C (W.addY x₁ x₂ y₁ (W.slope x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂)))

WeierstrassCurve.expDegree_rec (m : ℕ) :
  (WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (2 * (m + 3)) =
        2 * WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 2) + WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 3) +
          WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 5) ∧
      WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (2 * (m + 3)) =
        WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 1) + WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 3) +
          2 * WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 4)) ∧
    (WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (2 * (m + 2) + 1) =
        WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 4) + 3 * WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 2) + if Even m then 2 * 3 else 0) ∧
      WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (2 * (m + 2) + 1) =
        WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 1) + 3 * WeierstrassCurve.expDegree (m + 3) + if Even m then 0 else 2 * 3

WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff_rec (m : ℕ) :
  WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (2 * (m + 3)) =
      WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 2) ^ 2 * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 3) * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 5) -
        WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 1) * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 3) * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 4) ^ 2 ∧
    WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (2 * (m + 2) + 1) =
      (WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 4) * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 2) ^ 3 * if Even m then 4 ^ 2 else 1) -
        WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 1) * WeierstrassCurve.expCoeff (m + 3) ^ 3 * if Even m then 1 else 4 ^ 2

PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology.code: PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology.{u} {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] : TopologicalSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)
PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology.comment:
The Zariski topology on the prime spectrum of a commutative (semi)ring is defined
via the closed sets of the topology: they are exactly those sets that are the zero locus
of a subset of the ring.

explanatories.TopologicalSpace.ofClosed: This introduces a way to construct a topological space by defining its closed sets and ensuring they meet the necessary properties of closure under unions, intersections, and inclusion of the empty set.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.sInter_eq_iInter: The intersection of all sets in a collection is equal to the intersection of the individual sets in that collection.
explanatories.Subtype.prop: This theorem asserts that for a specific subtype, the property defining the subtype holds when applied to its element.
explanatories.PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_iUnion: The zero locus of the union of a collection of sets in a commutative semiring is equal to the intersection of the zero loci of each individual set in that collection.
explanatories.PrimeSpectrum.union_zeroLocus: The union of the zero loci of two sets is equal to the zero locus of the intersection of the ideals generated by those sets.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.

PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology.fullDefinition: instance zariskiTopology : TopologicalSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) :=   TopologicalSpace.ofClosed (Set.range PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus) ⟨Set.univ, by simp⟩     (by       intro Zs h       rw [Set.sInter_eq_iInter]       choose f hf using fun i : Zs => h i.prop       simp only [← hf]       exact ⟨_, zeroLocus_iUnion _⟩)     (by       rintro _ ⟨s, rfl⟩ _ ⟨t, rfl⟩       exact ⟨_, (union_zeroLocus s t).symm⟩)
PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology.description: This definition introduces the Zariski topology on the prime spectrum of a commutative semiring, where the closed sets correspond to the zero loci of subsets of the ring.

AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.isLocal.comment:
We will define the structure sheaf as
the subsheaf of all dependent functions in `Π x : U, Localizations R x`
consisting of those functions which can locally be expressed as a ratio of
(the images in the localization of) elements of `R`.

Quoting Hartshorne:

For an open set $U ⊆ Spec A$, we define $𝒪(U)$ to be the set of functions
$s : U → ⨆_{𝔭 ∈ U} A_𝔭$, such that $s(𝔭) ∈ A_𝔭$ for each $𝔭$,
and such that $s$ is locally a quotient of elements of $A$:
to be precise, we require that for each $𝔭 ∈ U$, there is a neighborhood $V$ of $𝔭$,
contained in $U$, and elements $a, f ∈ A$, such that for each $𝔮 ∈ V, f ∉ 𝔮$,
and $s(𝔮) = a/f$ in $A_𝔮$.

Now Hartshorne had the disadvantage of not knowing about dependent functions,
so we replace his circumlocution about functions into a disjoint union with
`Π x : U, Localizations x`.

  (f : (x : ↥U) → Localizations R ↑x) :
  (isLocallyFraction R).pred f =
    ∀ (x : ↥U),
      ∃ V,
        ∃ (_ : ↑x ∈ V),
          ∃ i r s,
            ∀ (y : ↥V),
              s ∉ (↑y).asIdeal ∧
                f ((fun x => ⟨↑x, ⋯⟩) y) * (algebraMap R (Localizations R ↑((fun x => ⟨↑x, ⋯⟩) y))) s =
                  (algebraMap R (Localizations R ↑((fun x => ⟨↑x, ⋯⟩) y))) r

AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.section.fullDefinition: def sectionsSubring (U : (Opens (PrimeSpectrum.Top R))ᵒᵖ) :     Subring (∀ x : U.unop, Localizations R x) where   carrier := { f | (isLocallyFraction R).pred f }   zero_mem' := by     refine fun x => ⟨unop U, x.2, 𝟙 _, 0, 1, fun y => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · rw [← Ideal.ne_top_iff_one]; exact y.1.isPrime.1     · simp   one_mem' := by     refine fun x => ⟨unop U, x.2, 𝟙 _, 1, 1, fun y => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · rw [← Ideal.ne_top_iff_one]; exact y.1.isPrime.1     · simp   add_mem' := by     intro a b ha hb x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases hb x with ⟨Vb, mb, ib, rb, sb, wb⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vb, ⟨ma, mb⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia, ra * sb + rb * sa, sa * sb, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wb (Opens.infLERight _ _ y) with ⟨nmb, wb⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [add_mul, RingHom.map_add, Pi.add_apply, RingHom.map_mul]       erw [← wa, ← wb]       simp only [mul_assoc]       congr 2       rw [mul_comm]   neg_mem' := by     intro a ha x     rcases ha x with ⟨V, m, i, r, s, w⟩     refine ⟨V, m, i, -r, s, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases w y with ⟨nm, w⟩     fconstructor     · exact nm     · simp only [RingHom.map_neg, Pi.neg_apply]       erw [← w]       simp only [neg_mul]   mul_mem' := by     intro a b ha hb x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases hb x with ⟨Vb, mb, ib, rb, sb, wb⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vb, ⟨ma, mb⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia, ra * rb, sa * sb, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wb (Opens.infLERight _ _ y) with ⟨nmb, wb⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [Pi.mul_apply, RingHom.map_mul]       erw [← wa, ← wb]       simp only [mul_left_comm, mul_assoc, mul_comm]

algebraic_geometry.structure_sheaf.secti.fullDefinition: def sectionsSubring (U : (Opens (PrimeSpectrum.Top R))ᵒᵖ) :     Subring (∀ x : U.unop, Localizations R x) where   carrier := { f | (isLocallyFraction R).pred f }   zero_mem' := by     refine fun x => ⟨unop U, x.2, 𝟙 _, 0, 1, fun y => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · rw [← Ideal.ne_top_iff_one]; exact y.1.isPrime.1     · simp   one_mem' := by     refine fun x => ⟨unop U, x.2, 𝟙 _, 1, 1, fun y => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · rw [← Ideal.ne_top_iff_one]; exact y.1.isPrime.1     · simp   add_mem' := by     intro a b ha hb x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases hb x with ⟨Vb, mb, ib, rb, sb, wb⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vb, ⟨ma, mb⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia, ra * sb + rb * sa, sa * sb, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wb (Opens.infLERight _ _ y) with ⟨nmb, wb⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [add_mul, RingHom.map_add, Pi.add_apply, RingHom.map_mul]       erw [← wa, ← wb]       simp only [mul_assoc]       congr 2       rw [mul_comm]   neg_mem' := by     intro a ha x     rcases ha x with ⟨V, m, i, r, s, w⟩     refine ⟨V, m, i, -r, s, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases w y with ⟨nm, w⟩     fconstructor     · exact nm     · simp only [RingHom.map_neg, Pi.neg_apply]       erw [← w]       simp only [neg_mul]   mul_mem' := by     intro a b ha hb x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases hb x with ⟨Vb, mb, ib, rb, sb, wb⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vb, ⟨ma, mb⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia, ra * rb, sa * sb, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wb (Opens.infLERight _ _ y) with ⟨nmb, wb⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [Pi.mul_apply, RingHom.map_mul]       erw [← wa, ← wb]       simp only [mul_left_comm, mul_assoc, mul_comm]

explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.res_app: This theorem states that applying a restriction of the structure sheaf along a morphism between open sets yields an equality involving the pushforward of the section at a point in the target open set.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.const_a: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the constant function defined on an open subset of the prime spectrum and its representation in the localization of a commutative ring, under the condition that one of the constants does not belong to the prime ideal associated with any point in that subset.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.exists_: This theorem guarantees the existence of a neighborhood around a point in the open set of the prime spectrum, where a constant function can be expressed in terms of a given local section from the structure sheaf, alongside conditions related to the ideal associated with that point.
explanatories.PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen: This definition characterizes the basic open sets in the prime spectrum of a commutative semiring as those containing all prime ideals that do not include a specific element from the ring.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.res_con: This theorem asserts that a specific map of the structure sheaf evaluated at a basic open set is equal to a constant function evaluated over a larger open set contained within the basic open set.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.stalk: The definition describes how to determine the stalk of a presheaf at a given point by taking the colimit of a functor that maps neighborhoods of that point to the values of the presheaf.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.localiz: This definition establishes a canonical ring homomorphism that connects the localization of a commutative ring at a prime ideal to the stalk of the structure sheaf at the corresponding point in the prime spectrum.
This theorem shows that the localization of a ring at a prime ideal's complement corresponds to the stalk of the structure sheaf at the associated point in the prime spectrum.

This theorem establishes a relationship between the localization at a prime ideal and the germ of a section of the structure sheaf at that prime, indicating that the localization operation corresponds to evaluating the germ of the section at a certain point associated with the prime ideal.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.stalkTo: This definition describes a ring homomorphism that connects the stalk of the structure sheaf at a prime ideal with the localization of the ring at that ideal through a process of gluing local sections.

This theorem establishes that the mapping from the stalk of the structure sheaf at a point to the fiber of the corresponding ring homomorphism preserves the germ of a section when evaluated at that point.

This theorem asserts that applying a certain mapping associated with the stalk of a prime ideal to an element of the ring yields an image that corresponds to the algebraic map from the original ring to its localization at that prime ideal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.comp_apply: This theorem asserts that the composition of two morphisms in a concrete category is equivalent to applying the second morphism to the result of the first morphism when evaluated at an object from the underlying type.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ_ext: The theorem establishes that if two sections of a presheaf agree on a neighborhood from which they are pulled back to a common open set, then their germ representations at a specific point in that open set are also equal.
explanatories.IsLocalization.ringHom_ext: The theorem states that if two ring homomorphisms from a localized structure into another commutative ring agree when composed with the algebra map from the original commutative semiring, then the two homomorphisms must be identical.
explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.RingHom.comp_apply: This theorem asserts that the composition of two ring homomorphisms applied to an element is equal to the application of the second homomorphism followed by the application of the first homomorphism.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.RingHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two ring homomorphisms are equal if they yield the same output for every input from the domain.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.

AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.stalkIs.fullDefinition: def stalkIso (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R) :     (structureSheaf R).presheaf.stalk x ≅ CommRingCat.of (Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal) where   hom := stalkToFiberRingHom R x   inv := localizationToStalk R x   hom_inv_id := by     ext U hxU s     -- Note: this `simp` was longer, but the line below had to become an `erw`     simp only [Category.comp_id]     erw [comp_apply, comp_apply, stalkToFiberRingHom_germ']     obtain ⟨V, hxV, iVU, f, g, (hg : V ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen _), hs⟩ :=       exists_const _ _ s x hxU     erw [← res_apply R U V iVU s ⟨x, hxV⟩, ← hs, const_apply, localizationToStalk_mk']     refine (structureSheaf R).presheaf.germ_ext V hxV (homOfLE hg) iVU ?_     dsimp     erw [← hs, res_const']   inv_hom_id :=     @IsLocalization.ringHom_ext R _ x.asIdeal.primeCompl (Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal) _ _       (Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal) _ _       (RingHom.comp (stalkToFiberRingHom R x) (localizationToStalk R x))       (RingHom.id (Localization.AtPrime _)) <| by         ext f         -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644         rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.comp_apply]; erw [localizationToStalk_of,           stalkToFiberRingHom_toStalk]; rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.id_apply]
AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.stalkIs.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the stalk of the structure sheaf at a prime ideal and the localization of the corresponding commutative ring at that prime ideal.

explanatories.IsLocalization.mk': This definition describes a surjective function that maps pairs of an element from a commutative semiring and an element from a submonoid to the target commutative semiring by taking their product and inverting the latter element.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.const: This definition describes a section of the structure sheaf associated with a commutative ring that maps each point in an open subset of its prime spectrum to the localization of the ring at that point, using the ratio of two ring elements provided that the denominator is not in the associated prime ideal.

AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comapFu.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comapFun.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type u} [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
  (U : Opens ↑(PrimeSpectrum.Top R)) (V : Opens ↑(PrimeSpectrum.Top S))
  (hUV : V.carrier ⊆ ⇑(PrimeSpectrum.comap f) ⁻¹' U.carrier) (s : (x : ↥U) → Localizations R ↑x) (y : ↥V) :
  Localizations S ↑y
AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comapFu.comment:
Given a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S`, an open set `U` of the prime spectrum of `R` and an open
set `V` of the prime spectrum of `S`, such that `V ⊆ (comap f) ⁻¹' U`, we can push a section `s`
on `U` to a section on `V`, by composing with `Localization.localRingHom _ _ f` from the left and
`comap f` from the right. Explicitly, if `s` evaluates on `comap f p` to `a / b`, its image on `V`
evaluates on `p` to `f(a) / f(b)`.

At the moment, we work with arbitrary dependent functions `s : Π x : U, Localizations R x`. Below,
we prove the predicate `isLocallyFraction` is preserved by this map, hence it can be extended to
a morphism between the structure sheaves of `R` and `S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comap.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comap.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type u} [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
  (U : Opens ↑(PrimeSpectrum.Top R)) (V : Opens ↑(PrimeSpectrum.Top S))
  (hUV : V.carrier ⊆ ⇑(PrimeSpectrum.comap f) ⁻¹' U.carrier) :
  ↑((structureSheaf R).val.obj (op U)) →+* ↑((structureSheaf S).val.obj (op V))
AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.comap.comment:
For a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S` and open sets `U` and `V` of the prime spectra of `R` and
`S` such that `V ⊆ (comap f) ⁻¹ U`, the induced ring homomorphism from the structure sheaf of `R`
at `U` to the structure sheaf of `S` at `V`.

Explicitly, this map is given as follows: For a point `p : V`, if the section `s` evaluates on `p`
to the fraction `a / b`, its image on `V` evaluates on `p` to the fraction `f(a) / f(b)`.

rfl     have :=       (@IsLocalization.mk'_one _ _ _ _ _ _             (StructureSheaf.IsLocalization.to_basicOpen S <| algebraMap R S r) x).trans         this     obtain ⟨⟨_, n, rfl⟩, e⟩ := (IsLocalization.mk'_eq_zero_iff _ _).mp this     refine ⟨⟨r, hpr⟩ ^ n, ?_⟩     rw [Submonoid.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def]     -- Porting note: manually rewrite `Submonoid.coe_pow`     change (algebraMap R S) (r ^ n) * x = 0     rw [map_pow]     exact e set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

explanatories.CommRingCat: This definition refers to the category consisting of commutative rings and their morphisms.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.topMap: The definition describes the induced map from a ring homomorphism on the spectra of rings, represented as a morphism between their corresponding topological spaces.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.Opens.map: This definition describes a functor that maps open sets from one topological space to another by taking the preimage of those sets under a given continuous function.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.sheafedSpaceMap: The definition describes the induced morphism between sheafed spaces corresponding to a ring homomorphism between their respective commutative rings.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen: This definition characterizes the basic open sets in the prime spectrum of a commutative semiring as those containing all prime ideals that do not include a specific element from the ring.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toOpen: This definition specifies a canonical ring homomorphism that associates elements of a commutative ring with sections of the corresponding structure sheaf over an open subset of the prime spectrum.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.Hom.c: This definition describes a morphism between presheaves that is induced by a given morphism between presheafed spaces, effectively linking their associated structures in a categorical context.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.comp_apply: This theorem asserts that the composition of two morphisms in a concrete category is equivalent to applying the second morphism to the result of the first morphism when evaluated at an object from the underlying type.
explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.stalk: The definition describes how to determine the stalk of a presheaf at a given point by taking the colimit of a functor that maps neighborhoods of that point to the values of the presheaf.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ: The definition describes how to obtain the germ of a section of a presheaf at a point within an open set, providing a morphism from the section to the stalk at that point.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toPushf: This definition specifies a ring homomorphism from a commutative ring to the stalk of the pushforward of its structure sheaf at a prime ideal induced by a ring homomorphism between two commutative rings.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor: The definition introduces a functor that maps presheaves over a given space to objects in a category, utilizing the stalks of those presheaves.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toPushf: The theorem establishes a relationship between the composition of a pushforward stalk along a morphism of commutative rings and the stalk at a prime ideal, involving the corresponding morphism in sheafed spaces.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.algebra: The theorem states that the algebra map from a commutative ring to the stalk of the pushed forward structure sheaf at a prime ideal equals the composition of the ring homomorphism and the map to the pushed forward stalk.
explanatories.Ideal.primeCompl: The definition describes the complement of a prime ideal in a commutative semiring as a submonoid.
explanatories.PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_o: The theorem confirms that the set of basic open sets, formed by the range of a function that maps elements to their corresponding basic open sets, serves as a topological basis in the context of a commutative semiring.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.exis: If a point belongs to an open set in a topological space that is covered by a topological basis, then there exists a basis element that contains the point and is also a subset of the open set.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.IsLocal: This definition indicates that the sections of the structure sheaf for a basic open set in the prime spectrum correspond to the localization of the ring at a specific element.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Submonoid.smul_def: The action of scalar multiplication by an element of a submonoid is equivalent to the same scalar multiplication by that element regarded as a member of the underlying monoid.
explanatories.Algebra.smul_def: This theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of an element in an algebra by a scalar from a commutative semiring can be expressed as the product of the image of that scalar under the algebra map and the algebra element.
explanatories.map_pow: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.isLocal: The theorem asserts the existence of an element in a localized module such that its action on a specified stalk related to a commutative ring morphism corresponds to a pushforward algebra homomorphism at a prime ideal.
explanatories.AlgHom.toLinearMap: This definition establishes a conversion from an algebra homomorphism to a linear map, facilitating the transition between algebraic structures over a commutative semiring and linear mappings.
explanatories.IsLocalizedModule.mkOfAlgebra: This theorem establishes that a given algebra homomorphism, under specific unit and linearity conditions, leads to the construction of a localized module associated with a submonoid.
explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map_units: The theorem states that the image of the algebra map from a commutative semiring to another, when applied to any element from a specific submonoid, is always a unit in the target semiring.
explanatories.IsUnit.map: An additive homomorphism defined on units can be derived from an additive homomorphism operating between two additive monoids.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toPushf: The definition outlines a homomorphism from a commutative ring to the stalk of a structure sheaf associated with the pushforward of that ring under a ring homomorphism and evaluated at a prime ideal.
The theorem expresses that the application of the ring homomorphism to a given element in the pushed forward structure sheaf at a prime ideal can be computed using the germ at that prime ideal.
explanatories.RingHom.map_zero: This theorem establishes that a ring homomorphism must send the additive identity from the domain to the additive identity in the codomain.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.TopCat.Presheaf.germ_eq: The theorem states that if two sections of a presheaf at neighborhoods of a point are equal, then there exists a neighborhood around that point where these sections can be related through appropriate morphisms of the presheaf.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op_map: The theorem shows that the mapping of a morphism in the opposite category under a functor corresponds to the application of the functor to the unopposed version of that morphism, followed by taking the opposite of the result.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.toOpen_: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of the restriction of the structure sheaf to an open set and the map between two open sets is equivalent to the restriction of the structure sheaf to the larger open set.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk'_one: The theorem states that the image of an element from a semiring under the algebra map is equal to the localization of that element paired with the identity element in the target semiring.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk'_eq_zero_iff: The theorem states that a localized element is equal to zero if and only if there exists a submonoid element such that its product with the original element results in zero.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isFraction.code:
ModuleCat.Tilde.isFraction.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat R) {U : Opens (PrimeSpectrum R)}
  (f : (𝔭 : ↥U) → Localizations M ↑𝔭) : Prop
ModuleCat.Tilde.isFraction.comment:
For any open subset `U ⊆ Spec R`, `IsFraction` is the predicate expressing that a function
`f : ∏_{x ∈ U}, Mₓ` is such that for any `𝔭 ∈ U`, `f 𝔭 = m / s` for some `m : M` and `s ∉ 𝔭`.
In short `f` is a fraction on `U`.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isFraction.fullDefinition: def isFraction {U : Opens (PrimeSpectrum R)} (f : ∀ 𝔭 : U, Localizations M 𝔭.1) : Prop :=   ∃ (m : M) (s : R),     ∀ x : U, ¬s ∈ x.1.asIdeal ∧ s • f x = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M m
ModuleCat.Tilde.isFraction.description: This definition indicates that a function defined on an open subset of the prime spectrum of a ring behaves like a fraction with a numerator from the module and a denominator not contained in the prime ideal associated with each point in the subset.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isFractionPrelocal.comment: The property of a function `f : ∏_{x ∈ U}, Mₓ` being a fraction is stable under restriction.

explanatories.TopCat.PrelocalPredicate.pred: A prelocal predicate defines a property based on an underlying condition evaluated for elements within a specified open subset of a space.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isFractionPrelocal.fullDefinition: def isFractionPrelocal : PrelocalPredicate (Localizations M) where   pred {U} f := isFraction M f   res := by rintro V U i f ⟨m, s, w⟩; exact ⟨m, s, fun x => w (i x)⟩
ModuleCat.Tilde.isFractionPrelocal.description: This definition asserts that the property of a function being a fraction can be preserved when the function is restricted to a smaller domain within the context of localizations of a module.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isLocallyFraction.code: ModuleCat.Tilde.isLocallyFraction.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat R) : LocalPredicate (Localizations M)
ModuleCat.Tilde.isLocallyFraction.comment:
For any open subset `U ⊆ Spec R`, `IsLocallyFraction` is the predicate expressing that a function
`f : ∏_{x ∈ U}, Mₓ` is such that for any `𝔭 ∈ U`, there exists an open neighbourhood `V ∋ 𝔭`, such
that for any `𝔮 ∈ V`, `f 𝔮 = m / s` for some `m : M` and `s ∉ 𝔮`.
In short `f` is locally a fraction on `U`.

explanatories.TopCat.PrelocalPredicate.sheafify: A prelocal predicate can be transformed into a local predicate by requiring that its condition is satisfied in the neighborhoods around every point.

ModuleCat.Tilde.isLocallyFraction.description: This definition characterizes a function as being locally a fraction on an open subset of the prime spectrum of a ring if, for each point, there exists a neighborhood where the function can be expressed as a fraction with a numerator from the module and a denominator not contained in the prime ideal associated with any point in that neighborhood.

ModuleCat.tildeInType.comment:
For any `R`-module `M`, `TildeInType R M` is the sheaf of set on `Spec R` whose sections on `U` are

See also `Tilde.isLocallyFraction`.

ModuleCat.Tilde.sectionsSubmodule.fullDefinition: def sectionsSubmodule (U : (Opens (PrimeSpectrum R))ᵒᵖ) :     Submodule ((Spec.structureSheaf R).1.obj U) (∀ x : U.unop, Localizations M x.1) where   carrier := { f | (isLocallyFraction M).pred f }   zero_mem' x := ⟨unop U, x.2, 𝟙 _, 0, 1, fun y =>     ⟨Ideal.ne_top_iff_one _ |>.1 y.1.isPrime.1, by simp⟩⟩   add_mem' := by     intro a b ha hb x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases hb x with ⟨Vb, mb, ib, rb, sb, wb⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vb, ⟨ma, mb⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia,  sb• ra+ sa•rb , sa * sb, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y : Va) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wb (Opens.infLERight _ _ y : Vb) with ⟨nmb, wb⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [Opens.coe_inf, Pi.add_apply, smul_add, map_add,         LinearMapClass.map_smul] at wa wb ⊢       rw [← wa, ← wb, ← mul_smul, ← mul_smul]       congr 2       simp [mul_comm]   smul_mem' := by     intro r a ha x     rcases ha x with ⟨Va, ma, ia, ra, sa, wa⟩     rcases r.2 x with ⟨Vr, mr, ir, rr, sr, wr⟩     refine ⟨Va ⊓ Vr, ⟨ma, mr⟩, Opens.infLELeft _ _ ≫ ia, rr•ra, sr*sa, ?_⟩     intro y     rcases wa (Opens.infLELeft _ _ y : Va) with ⟨nma, wa⟩     rcases wr (Opens.infLERight _ _ y) with ⟨nmr, wr⟩     fconstructor     · intro H; cases y.1.isPrime.mem_or_mem H <;> contradiction     · simp only [Opens.coe_inf, Pi.smul_apply, LinearMapClass.map_smul] at wa wr ⊢       rw [mul_comm, ← Algebra.smul_def] at wr       rw [sections_smul_localizations_def, ← wa, ← mul_smul, ← smul_assoc, mul_comm sr, mul_smul,         wr, mul_comm rr, Algebra.smul_def, ← map_mul]       rfl

algebraic_geometry.Scheme.restrict_map_i.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev Scheme.restrictMapIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f]     (U : Opens Y) : X ∣_ᵤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U ≅ Y ∣_ᵤ U := by   apply IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq (f := X.ofRestrict _ ≫ f) (Y.ofRestrict _) _   dsimp [restrict]   rw [Set.range_comp, Subtype.range_val, Subtype.range_coe]   refine @Set.image_preimage_eq _ _ f.1.base U.1 ?_   rw [← TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]   infer_instance

AlgebraicGeometry.morphismRestrictStalkM.fullDefinition: def morphismRestrictStalkMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (U : Opens Y) (x) :     Arrow.mk (PresheafedSpace.stalkMap (f ∣_ U).1 x) ≅       Arrow.mk (PresheafedSpace.stalkMap f.1 x.1) := by   fapply Arrow.isoMk'   · refine Y.restrictStalkIso U.openEmbedding ((f ∣_ U).1.1 x) ≪≫ TopCat.Presheaf.stalkCongr _ ?_     apply Inseparable.of_eq     exact morphismRestrict_base_coe f U x   · exact X.restrictStalkIso (Opens.openEmbedding _) _   · apply TopCat.Presheaf.stalk_hom_ext     intro V hxV     change ↑(f ⁻¹ᵁ U) at x     simp only [Scheme.restrict_presheaf_obj, unop_op, Opens.coe_inclusion, Iso.trans_hom,       TopCat.Presheaf.stalkCongr_hom, Category.assoc, Scheme.restrict_toPresheafedSpace]     rw [PresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso_hom_eq_germ_assoc,       TopCat.Presheaf.germ_stalkSpecializes'_assoc,       PresheafedSpace.stalkMap_germ'_assoc, PresheafedSpace.stalkMap_germ',       ← Scheme.Hom.app, ← Scheme.Hom.app, morphismRestrict_app,       PresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso_hom_eq_germ, Category.assoc, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res]     rfl

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.bind.fullDefinition: def OpenCover.bind (f : ∀ x : 𝒰.J, OpenCover (𝒰.obj x)) : OpenCover X where   J := Σ i : 𝒰.J, (f i).J   obj x := (f x.1).obj x.2   map x := (f x.1).map x.2 ≫ 𝒰.map x.1   f x := ⟨_, (f _).f (𝒰.covers x).choose⟩   covers x := by     let y := (𝒰.covers x).choose     have hy : (𝒰.map (𝒰.f x)).val.base y = x := (𝒰.covers x).choose_spec     rcases (f (𝒰.f x)).covers y with ⟨z, hz⟩     change x ∈ Set.range ((f (𝒰.f x)).map ((f (𝒰.f x)).f y) ≫ 𝒰.map (𝒰.f x)).1.base     use z     erw [comp_apply]     erw [hz, hy] -- now `erw` after #13170   -- Porting note: weirdly, even though no input is needed, `inferInstance` does not work   -- `PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.comp` is marked as `instance`   IsOpen x := PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.comp _ _

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.copy.fullDefinition: def OpenCover.copy {X : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : OpenCover X) (J : Type*) (obj : J → Scheme)     (map : ∀ i, obj i ⟶ X) (e₁ : J ≃ 𝒰.J) (e₂ : ∀ i, obj i ≅ 𝒰.obj (e₁ i))     (e₂ : ∀ i, map i = (e₂ i).hom ≫ 𝒰.map (e₁ i)) : OpenCover X :=   { J, obj, map     f := fun x => e₁.symm (𝒰.f x)     covers := fun x => by       rw [e₂, Scheme.comp_val_base, TopCat.coe_comp, Set.range_comp, Set.range_iff_surjective.mpr,         Set.image_univ, e₁.rightInverse_symm]       · exact 𝒰.covers x       · erw [← TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]; infer_instance -- now `erw` after #13170     -- Porting note: weirdly, even though no input is needed, `inferInstance` does not work     -- `PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.comp` is marked as `instance`     IsOpen := fun i => by rw [e₂]; exact PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.comp _ _ }

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.finit.fullDefinition: def OpenCover.finiteSubcover {X : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : OpenCover X) [H : CompactSpace X] :     OpenCover X := by   have :=     @CompactSpace.elim_nhds_subcover _ _ H (fun x : X => Set.range (𝒰.map (𝒰.f x)).1.base)       fun x => (IsOpenImmersion.isOpen_range (𝒰.map (𝒰.f x))).mem_nhds (𝒰.covers x)   let t := this.choose   have h : ∀ x : X, ∃ y : t, x ∈ Set.range (𝒰.map (𝒰.f y)).1.base := by     intro x     have h' : x ∈ (⊤ : Set X) := trivial     rw [← Classical.choose_spec this, Set.mem_iUnion] at h'     rcases h' with ⟨y, _, ⟨hy, rfl⟩, hy'⟩     exact ⟨⟨y, hy⟩, hy'⟩   exact     { J := t       obj := fun x => 𝒰.obj (𝒰.f x.1)       map := fun x => 𝒰.map (𝒰.f x.1)       f := fun x => (h x).choose       covers := fun x => (h x).choose_spec }

algebraic_geometry.Scheme.open_cover.int.fullDefinition: def OpenCover.inter {X : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰₁ : Scheme.OpenCover.{v₁} X)     (𝒰₂ : Scheme.OpenCover.{v₂} X) : X.OpenCover where   J := 𝒰₁.J × 𝒰₂.J   obj ij := pullback (𝒰₁.map ij.1) (𝒰₂.map ij.2)   map ij := pullback.fst _ _ ≫ 𝒰₁.map ij.1   f x := ⟨𝒰₁.f x, 𝒰₂.f x⟩   covers x := by     rw [IsOpenImmersion.range_pullback_to_base_of_left]     exact ⟨𝒰₁.covers x, 𝒰₂.covers x⟩   IsOpen x := inferInstance

AlgebraicGeometry.identityToΓSpec.fullDefinition: def identityToΓSpec : 𝟭 LocallyRingedSpace.{u} ⟶ Γ.rightOp ⋙ Spec.toLocallyRingedSpace where   app := LocallyRingedSpace.toΓSpec   naturality X Y f := by     symm     apply LocallyRingedSpace.comp_ring_hom_ext     · ext1 x       dsimp only [Spec.topMap, LocallyRingedSpace.toΓSpecFun]       -- Porting note: Had to add the next four lines       rw [comp_apply]       dsimp [toΓSpecBase]       -- The next six lines were `rw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk, ContinuousMap.coe_mk]` before       -- leanprover/lean4#2644       have : (ContinuousMap.mk (toΓSpecFun Y) (toΓSpec_continuous _)) (f.val.base x)         = toΓSpecFun Y (f.val.base x) := by rw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk]       erw [this]       have : (ContinuousMap.mk (toΓSpecFun X) (toΓSpec_continuous _)) x         = toΓSpecFun X x := by rw [ContinuousMap.coe_mk]       erw [this]       dsimp [toΓSpecFun]       -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644       erw [← LocalRing.comap_closedPoint (PresheafedSpace.stalkMap f.val x), ←         PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp_apply, ← PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp_apply]       congr 2       exact (PresheafedSpace.stalkMap_germ f.1 ⊤ ⟨x, trivial⟩).symm     · intro r       rw [LocallyRingedSpace.comp_val_c_app, ← Category.assoc]       erw [Y.toΓSpecSheafedSpace_app_spec, f.1.c.naturality]       rfl

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.glueM.comment:
Given an open cover of `X`, and a morphism `𝒰.obj x ⟶ Y` for each open subscheme in the cover,
such that these morphisms are compatible in the intersection (pullback), we may glue the morphisms
together into a morphism `X ⟶ Y`.

Note:
If `X` is exactly (defeq to) the gluing of `U i`, then using `Multicoequalizer.desc` suffices.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.glueM.fullDefinition: def glueMorphisms {Y : Scheme} (f : ∀ x, 𝒰.obj x ⟶ Y)     (hf : ∀ x y, pullback.fst (𝒰.map x) (𝒰.map y) ≫ f x = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ f y) :     X ⟶ Y := by   refine inv 𝒰.fromGlued ≫ ?_   fapply Multicoequalizer.desc   · exact f   rintro ⟨i, j⟩   change pullback.fst _ _ ≫ f i = (_ ≫ _) ≫ f j   erw [pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_fst]   exact hf i j

AlgebraicGeometry.of_affine_open_cover.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.of_affine_open_cover.{u_1, u_2} {X : Scheme} {P : ↑X.affineOpens → Prop} {ι : Sort u_2}
  (U : ι → ↑X.affineOpens) (iSup_U : ⨆ i, ↑(U i) = ⊤) (V : ↑X.affineOpens)
  (basicOpen : ∀ (U : ↑X.affineOpens) (f : ↑Γ(X, ↑U)), P U → P (X.affineBasicOpen f))
  (openCover :
    ∀ (U : ↑X.affineOpens) (s : Finset ↑Γ(X, ↑U)),
      Ideal.span ↑s = ⊤ → (∀ (f : { x // x ∈ s }), P (X.affineBasicOpen ↑f)) → P U)
  (hU : ∀ (i : ι), P (U i)) : P V
AlgebraicGeometry.of_affine_open_cover.comment:
Let `P` be a predicate on the affine open sets of `X` satisfying
1. If `P` holds on `U`, then `P` holds on the basic open set of every section on `U`.
2. If `P` holds for a family of basic open sets covering `U`, then `P` holds for `U`.
3. There exists an affine open cover of `X` each satisfying `P`.

Then `P` holds for every affine open of `X`.

AlgebraicGeometry.of_affine_open_cover.{u_1, u_2} {X : Scheme} {P : ↑X.affineOpens → Prop} {ι : Sort u_2}
  (U : ι → ↑X.affineOpens) (iSup_U : ⨆ i, ↑(U i) = ⊤) (V : ↑X.affineOpens)
  (basicOpen : ∀ (U : ↑X.affineOpens) (f : ↑Γ(X, ↑U)), P U → P (X.affineBasicOpen f))
  (openCover :
    ∀ (U : ↑X.affineOpens) (s : Finset ↑Γ(X, ↑U)),
      Ideal.span ↑s = ⊤ → (∀ (f : { x // x ∈ s }), P (X.affineBasicOpen ↑f)) → P U)
  (hU : ∀ (i : ι), P (U i)) : P V
algebraic_geometry.of_affine_open_cover.comment:
Let `P` be a predicate on the affine open sets of `X` satisfying
1. If `P` holds on `U`, then `P` holds on the basic open set of every section on `U`.
2. If `P` holds for a family of basic open sets covering `U`, then `P` holds for `U`.
3. There exists an affine open cover of `X` each satisfying `P`.

Then `P` holds for every affine open of `X`.

This is also known as the **Affine communication lemma** in [*The rising sea*][RisingSea].

AlgebraicGeometry.reduce_to_affine_globa.comment:
To show that a statement `P` holds for all open subsets of all schemes, it suffices to show that
1. In any scheme `X`, if `P` holds for an open cover of `U`, then `P` holds for `U`.
2. For an open immerison `f : X ⟶ Y`, if `P` holds for the entire space of `X`, then `P` holds for
  the image of `f`.
3. `P` holds for the entire space of an affine scheme.

AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_of_is.fullDefinition: instance irreducibleSpace_of_isIntegral [IsIntegral X] : IrreducibleSpace X := by   by_contra H   replace H : ¬IsPreirreducible (⊤ : Set X) := fun h =>     H { toPreirreducibleSpace := ⟨h⟩         toNonempty := inferInstance }   simp_rw [isPreirreducible_iff_closed_union_closed, not_forall, not_or] at H   rcases H with ⟨S, T, hS, hT, h₁, h₂, h₃⟩   erw [not_forall] at h₂ h₃   simp_rw [not_forall] at h₂ h₃   haveI : Nonempty (⟨Sᶜ, hS.1⟩ : Opens X) := ⟨⟨_, h₂.choose_spec.choose_spec⟩⟩   haveI : Nonempty (⟨Tᶜ, hT.1⟩ : Opens X) := ⟨⟨_, h₃.choose_spec.choose_spec⟩⟩   haveI : Nonempty (⟨Sᶜ, hS.1⟩ ⊔ ⟨Tᶜ, hT.1⟩ : Opens X) :=     ⟨⟨_, Or.inl h₂.choose_spec.choose_spec⟩⟩   let e : Γ(X, _) ≅ CommRingCat.of _ :=     (X.sheaf.isProductOfDisjoint ⟨_, hS.1⟩ ⟨_, hT.1⟩ ?_).conePointUniqueUpToIso       (CommRingCat.prodFanIsLimit _ _)   · apply (config := { allowSynthFailures := true }) false_of_nontrivial_of_product_domain     · exact e.symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isDomain _     · apply X.toLocallyRingedSpace.component_nontrivial     · apply X.toLocallyRingedSpace.component_nontrivial   · ext x     constructor     · rintro ⟨hS, hT⟩       cases' h₁ (show x ∈ ⊤ by trivial) with h h       exacts [hS h, hT h]     · intro x       exact x.rec (by contradiction)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.t_fst_: This theorem asserts that a specific composition involving pullback morphisms and a supplementary morphism behaves consistently with the structure of the pullback in the associated schemes.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.condi: The theorem asserts that in a pullback cone, the composition of the first projection with its associated morphism matches the composition of the second projection with the other morphism in the cospan.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map: This definition specifies a morphism between the spectra of two commutative rings induced by a ring homomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd: This definition specifies the morphism from the pullback object to one of its original objects, representing the second projection of the pullback for a given pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map: This definition establishes a morphism between the pullbacks of two pairs of morphisms that share a common object, under specified conditions relating to their compositions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.pullb: This definition describes the process of creating an open cover of one scheme by pulling back an existing open cover from another scheme via a morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GlueData.V: This definition describes a morphism in a category that is associated with a pair of elements from the glue data structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.snd: The second projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the second object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.condi: The theorem asserts that in a pullback cone, the composition of the first projection with its associated morphism matches the composition of the second projection with the other morphism in the cospan.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map: This definition specifies a morphism between the spectra of two commutative rings induced by a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.fullDefinition: def gluedLiftPullbackMap (i j : 𝒰.J) :     pullback ((𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).map i) ((𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).map j) ⟶       (gluing 𝒰 f g).V ⟨i, j⟩ := by   refine (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso _ _ _).hom ≫ ?_   refine pullback.map _ _ _ _ ?_ (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) ?_ ?_   · exact (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom ≫       pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) s.snd f (Category.id_comp _).symm s.condition   · simpa using pullback.condition   · simp only [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.description: This definition introduces a morphism that relates the pullback of two mappings associated with an open cover to the gluing of schemes, enabling the construction of a coherent transition between local pieces.

algebraic_geometry.Scheme.pullback.glued.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedLiftPullbackMap.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (s : PullbackCone f g) (i j : 𝒰.J) :
  pullback ((𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).map i) ((𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).map j) ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).V (i, j)
algebraic_geometry.Scheme.pullback.glued.comment:
(Implementation)
The canonical map `(s.X ×[X] Uᵢ) ×[s.X] (s.X ×[X] Uⱼ) ⟶ (Uᵢ ×[Z] Y) ×[X] Uⱼ`

This is used in `gluedLift`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedLiftPullbackMap_fst.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z)
  (g : Y ⟶ Z) [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (s : PullbackCone f g) (i j : 𝒰.J) :
  gluedLiftPullbackMap 𝒰 f g s i j ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g ≫ 𝒰.map i) (𝒰.map j) =

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedLift.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (s : PullbackCone f g) : s.pt ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).glued
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.comment:
The lifted map `s.X ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).glued` in order to show that `(gluing 𝒰 f g).glued` is
indeed the pullback.

Given a pullback cone `s`, we have the maps `s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` and
`s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ s.X ⟶ Y` that we may lift to a map `s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`.

to glue these into a map `s.X ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`, we need to show that the maps agree on
`(s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ) ×[s.X] (s.fst ⁻¹' Uⱼ) ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`. This is achieved by showing that both of these
maps factors through `gluedLiftPullbackMap`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.fullDefinition: def gluedLift : s.pt ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).glued := by   fapply (𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).glueMorphisms   · exact fun i ↦ (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom ≫       pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) s.snd f (Category.id_comp _).symm s.condition ≫ (gluing 𝒰 f g).ι i   intro i j   rw [← gluedLiftPullbackMap_fst_assoc, ← gluing_f, ← (gluing 𝒰 f g).glue_condition i j,     gluing_t, gluing_f]   simp_rw [← Category.assoc]   congr 1   apply pullback.hom_ext <;> simp_rw [Category.assoc]   · rw [t_fst_fst, gluedLiftPullbackMap_snd]     congr 1     rw [← Iso.inv_comp_eq, pullbackSymmetry_inv_comp_snd, pullback.lift_fst, Category.comp_id]   · rw [t_fst_snd, gluedLiftPullbackMap_fst_assoc, pullback.lift_snd, pullback.lift_snd]     simp_rw [pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd_assoc]     exact pullback.condition_assoc _
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedL.description: This definition specifies a morphism arising from a pullback cone that relates a point in the pullback to the glued construction of a cover, enabling the verification that the glued object is indeed the pullback.

algebraic_geometry.Scheme.pullback.glued.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedLift.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (s : PullbackCone f g) : s.pt ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).glued
algebraic_geometry.Scheme.pullback.glued.comment:
The lifted map `s.X ⟶ (gluing 𝒰 f g).glued` in order to show that `(gluing 𝒰 f g).glued` is
indeed the pullback.

Given a pullback cone `s`, we have the maps `s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` and
`s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ s.X ⟶ Y` that we may lift to a map `s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`.

to glue these into a map `s.X ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`, we need to show that the maps agree on
`(s.fst ⁻¹' Uᵢ) ×[s.X] (s.fst ⁻¹' Uⱼ) ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y`. This is achieved by showing that both of these
maps factors through `gluedLiftPullbackMap`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.pullba.comment:
(Implementation)
The canonical map `(W ×[X] Uᵢ) ×[W] (Uⱼ ×[Z] Y) ⟶ (Uⱼ ×[Z] Y) ×[X] Uᵢ = V j i` where `W` is
the glued fibred product.

This is used in `lift_comp_ι`.

The canonical map `(W ×[X] Uᵢ) ×[W] (Uⱼ ×[Z] Y) ⟶ (Uⱼ ×[Z] Y) ×[X] Uᵢ = V j i` where `W` is
the glued fibred product.

This is used in `lift_comp_ι`.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.lift_c.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.lift_comp_ι.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (i : 𝒰.J) :
  pullback.lift (pullback.snd (p1 𝒰 f g) (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.fst (p1 𝒰 f g) (𝒰.map i) ≫ p2 𝒰 f g) ⋯ ≫
      (gluing 𝒰 f g).ι i =
    pullback.fst (p1 𝒰 f g) (𝒰.map i)
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.lift_c.comment:
We show that the map `W ×[X] Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ ×[Z] Y ⟶ W` is the first projection, where the
first map is given by the lift of `W ×[X] Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` and `W ×[X] Uᵢ ⟶ W ⟶ Y`.

It suffices to show that the two map agrees when restricted onto `Uⱼ ×[Z] Y`. In this case,
both maps factor through `V j i` via `pullback_fst_ι_to_V`

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.pullba.comment:
The canonical isomorphism between `W ×[X] Uᵢ` and `Uᵢ ×[X] Y`. That is, the preimage of `Uᵢ` in
`W` along `p1` is indeed `Uᵢ ×[X] Y`.

explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.map: This definition describes a mapping from a specific subscheme to a given scheme, representing the embedding of subschemes into that scheme.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback: This definition computes the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms that have a common target in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst: This definition describes the first projection map from the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms to the first object of one of the morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd: This definition specifies the morphism from the pullback object to one of its original objects, representing the second projection of the pullback for a given pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map: This definition establishes a morphism between the pullbacks of two pairs of morphisms that share a common object, under specified conditions relating to their compositions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem establishes a condition for a pullback, asserting that the composition of the first projection along a morphism must equal the composition of the second projection along the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift_snd: This theorem asserts that a specific morphism lifted from two given morphisms in a pullback construction, when composed with the second projection, equals the original morphism from the second object in the pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.hom_ext: Two morphisms into a pullback object are identical if their compositions with the projection morphisms from the pullback are identical.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.ι: This definition describes a morphism representing the immersion from a specified component of glue data into the resulting glued space.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.p1: This definition describes the first projection mapping from a glued scheme, constructed from an open cover, to the original scheme.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.p2: This definition specifies the second projection morphism from the glued scheme, formed from an open cover and two morphisms to a common scheme, into one of the original schemes.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicoequalizer.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a multicoequalizer to another object commute with the projections from the multicospan index, then those morphisms are equal.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.p_comm: This theorem asserts that the compositions of the first projection from the pullback into one scheme and the second projection into another scheme yield the same morphism into the common scheme.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.fst: The first projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the first object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.snd: The second projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the second object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluing: This definition describes a structure that represents the glued fibered product of two schemes over a common base scheme, as determined by an open cover.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift_fst: This theorem states that a specific morphism lifted from a pair of morphisms in a pullback construction, when composed with the first projection, equals the original morphism from the common source.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicoequalizer.π: This theorem asserts that a specific morphism derived from a multicospan structure, when composed with a designated descendant morphism, yields a consistent equality with the morphism defined by applying that structure to an element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift: This definition states that for morphisms from a common object to a target object that satisfy a compatibility condition, there exists a morphism from an intermediary object to the pullback object formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.hom_e: This theorem states that if two morphisms from a scheme are equal when composed with the morphisms of a given open cover, then the two morphisms themselves must be equal.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.lift_c: This theorem shows that a specific composition of pullback lifts and projections agrees with the first projection map from the pullback of two morphisms through an open cover.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluing: This theorem describes how the morphism associated with the gluing of two morphisms over an open cover relates to the projection of a multicoequalizer diagram at a specified index.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map: This definition specifies a morphism between the spectra of two commutative rings induced by a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.pullba.fullDefinition: def pullbackP1Iso (i : 𝒰.J) : pullback (p1 𝒰 f g) (𝒰.map i) ≅ pullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g := by   fconstructor   · exact       pullback.lift (pullback.snd _ _) (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ p2 𝒰 f g)         (by rw [← pullback.condition_assoc, Category.assoc, p_comm])   · apply pullback.lift ((gluing 𝒰 f g).ι i) (pullback.fst _ _)     rw [gluing_ι, p1, Multicoequalizer.π_desc]   · apply pullback.hom_ext     · simpa using lift_comp_ι 𝒰 f g i     · simp_rw [Category.assoc, pullback.lift_snd, pullback.lift_fst, Category.id_comp]   · apply pullback.hom_ext     · simp_rw [Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst, pullback.lift_snd, Category.id_comp]     · simp [p2]
AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.pullba.description: This definition establishes a canonical isomorphism between two pullback objects, relating the preimage of an open set under a specific projection to the pullback of that set along a given morphism.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedLift.eq_1.{u} {X Y Z : Scheme} (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [∀ (i : 𝒰.J), HasPullback (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g] (s : PullbackCone f g) :
  gluedLift 𝒰 f g s =
    (𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).glueMorphisms
      (fun i =>
        (pullbackSymmetry s.fst (𝒰.map i)).hom ≫
          pullback.map (𝒰.map i) s.fst (𝒰.map i ≫ f) g (𝟙 (𝒰.obj i)) s.snd f ⋯ ⋯ ≫ (gluing 𝒰 f g).ι i)
      ⋯

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.gluedI.fullDefinition: def gluedIsLimit : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ (p_comm 𝒰 f g)) := by   apply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   refine ⟨gluedLift 𝒰 f g s, gluedLift_p1 𝒰 f g s, gluedLift_p2 𝒰 f g s, ?_⟩   intro m h₁ h₂   simp_rw [PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app] at h₁ h₂   apply (𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).hom_ext   intro i   rw [gluedLift, (𝒰.pullbackCover s.fst).ι_glueMorphisms, 𝒰.pullbackCover_map]   rw [← cancel_epi     (pullbackRightPullbackFstIso (p1 𝒰 f g) (𝒰.map i) m ≪≫ pullback.congrHom h₁ rfl).hom,     Iso.trans_hom, Category.assoc, pullback.congrHom_hom, pullback.lift_fst_assoc,     Category.comp_id, pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_fst_assoc, pullback.condition]   conv_lhs => rhs; rw [← pullbackP1Iso_hom_ι]   simp_rw [← Category.assoc]   congr 1   apply pullback.hom_ext   · simp_rw [Category.assoc, pullbackP1Iso_hom_fst, pullback.lift_fst, Category.comp_id,       pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_fst, pullback.lift_snd, Category.comp_id,       pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_snd]   · simp_rw [Category.assoc, pullbackP1Iso_hom_snd, pullback.lift_snd,       pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd_assoc, pullback.lift_fst_assoc, Category.comp_id,       pullbackRightPullbackFstIso_hom_fst_assoc, ← pullback.condition_assoc, h₂]

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.

explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPullbac: The definition states that a larger square formed by composing two smaller squares is a pullback if both of the smaller squares are pullbacks themselves.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim: A pullback cone is demonstrated to be a limit cone if the cone obtained by flipping its projections is also a limit cone.

algebraic_geometry.Scheme.pullback.open_.fullDefinition: def openCoverOfBase' (𝒰 : OpenCover Z) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : OpenCover (pullback f g) := by   apply (openCoverOfLeft (𝒰.pullbackCover f) f g).bind   intro i   let Xᵢ := pullback f (𝒰.map i)   let Yᵢ := pullback g (𝒰.map i)   let W := pullback (pullback.snd _ _ : Yᵢ ⟶ _) (pullback.snd _ _ : Xᵢ ⟶ _)   have :=     bigSquareIsPullback (pullback.fst _ _ : W ⟶ _) (pullback.fst _ _ : Yᵢ ⟶ _)       (pullback.snd _ _ : Xᵢ ⟶ _) (𝒰.map i) (pullback.snd _ _) (pullback.snd _ _) g       pullback.condition.symm pullback.condition.symm       (PullbackCone.isLimitOfFlip <| pullbackIsPullback _ _)       (PullbackCone.isLimitOfFlip <| pullbackIsPullback _ _)   refine     @openCoverOfIsIso       (f := (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom ≫ (limit.isoLimitCone ⟨_, this⟩).inv ≫         pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) ?_ ?_) ?_   · simp [← pullback.condition]   · simp only [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]   · infer_instance

  (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  (x :
    (i : (openCoverOfLeft (𝒰.pullbackCover f) f g).J) ×
      ((fun i =>
            let Xᵢ := pullback f (𝒰.map i);
            let Yᵢ := pullback g (𝒰.map i);
            let W := pullback (pullback.snd g (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.snd f (𝒰.map i));
            let_fun this :=
              bigSquareIsPullback (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.snd f (𝒰.map i)))
                (pullback.fst g (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.snd f (𝒰.map i)) (𝒰.map i)
                (pullback.snd (pullback.snd g (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.snd f (𝒰.map i))) (pullback.snd g (𝒰.map i)) g ⋯ ⋯

            openCoverOfIsIso
              ((pullbackSymmetry (pullback.snd f (𝒰.map i)) (pullback.snd g (𝒰.map i))).hom ≫
                (limit.isoLimitCone
                      {
                        cone :=
